name: TC Electronic G-Force
source: TC Electronic G-Force User's Manual (English, Rev 1.01, SW 2.04, 'G-Force_US_270104'; Audiofanzine media 483323 = tcelectronic.com/media/216735) incl. MIDI implementation chart ('May 23th, 1997 Version 1.0'); G-Force Manual Addendum 1.05 -> 2.04 (tcelectronic.com/media/216761, via web.archive.org); G-Force service manual TOC (manualslib 2286300: no MIDI content). No TC SysEx document for the G-Force exists in TC's archive (the 2009/2013 support pages list only manuals/addendum/G-Card guide). Transport cross-checked against TC's FireworX MIDI specification V1.00 (same platform; its User Bank Header/Data Packet messages are the pre-2.00 bank format) and Christian Jacobsson's G-Force pages (sysex.htm: dump message sizes; software_versions.htm). No open-source G-Force editor exists (KnobKraft, Ctrlr, Edisyn, SoundDiver: none).

deviceId.rule: Byte 4 = the unit's 'Sysex device ID' (I/O Setup > MIDI). The manuals give no range; TC's siblings of this generation use 0-126 (G-System manual) with 127 unconfirmed as 'all'. Keep the editor and the unit on the same number (default 0). Replies carry the unit's own ID in byte 4.
deviceId.sweep: If a request gets no reply, the driver may sweep dev 0-126 with the same read-only request (one at a time, 300 ms each) and keep the first that answers (prefs 'dev'), like the Yamaha driver does.

tc.numbers14: Every 2-byte number (preset, count, address, size, packet count) is 14-bit, 7 bits per byte, MSB first: [n >> 7 & 7F, n & 7F].
tc.nibbles: Binary data travels as nibble pairs, high nibble first: byte b -> [b >> 4, b & 0F]. A dump of N data bytes is 2N nibble bytes followed by ONE checksum byte.
tc.checksum: checksum = (-(sum of the DATA BYTES)) & 7F -- computed over the reassembled 8-bit bytes, not over the nibble bytes (TC spec, 'Binary data'). Receiver check: (sum(data) + checksum) & 7F == 0.
tc.modelNote: UNKNOWN -- TC published no G-Force SysEx document (manual chart: System Exclusive 'O Bulkdump' only). FireworX = 40h (1998), M-One 44h, D-Two 45h; the G-Force (1997) predates them. Learn it: the first User Bank Header the unit sends (front-panel dump) carries it in byte 5; store it in prefs 'model'. Never guess one for transmission.

capabilities.paramWriteCC: Ext 1-8 (per-preset matrix links), main vol, overall bypass, tempo tap, tuner, 9 block bypasses
capabilities.bankBackup: whole user bank only, started on the front panel (Utility > User bank to MIDI); restore after arming Utility > MIDI to User bank
capabilities.transmitsEdits: no parameter data; transmits block bypass states on their CCs at preset change (1.13+), optional program-change re-transmit, tuner data for a G-Minor (format undocumented; keep Tuner MIDI Out off)

bankDump.observed: Christian Jacobsson's G-Force pages (christianjacobsson.se/g-force/sysex.htm): a user-bank dump shows in SysEx Solution 97 as one 9-byte message followed by a few hundred 137-byte messages; 136-byte lines mean a corrupted transfer; loading a corrupt file makes the G-Force erase all user presets; a full dump takes up to a minute.
bankDump.inferred: Those sizes are exactly the FireworX User Bank Header (F0 00 20 1F dd MM 10 nH nL F7 = 10 bytes) and Data Packet (F0 00 20 1F dd MM 11 id <128 nibbles> ck F7 = 138 bytes) minus one byte each -- consistent with that program not counting one framing byte. The FireworX spec says these two messages are the older, pre-2.00 TC bank format. So the G-Force very probably uses the same two messages with its own model ID MM: 64 data bytes per packet as nibbles, checksum (-sum(data)) & 7F. Treat as inferred; verify on the first captured dump (header byte 6 = 10, packets byte 6 = 11, length 138, checksums).
bankDump.contents: Packet payload = raw user-bank memory; per-preset layout undocumented. Keep the whole dump as an opaque .syx for backup/restore.

tc.unverifiedRequests: Untested and undocumented for the G-Force: after the model ID is known, F0 00 20 1F dd MM 40 F7 (FireworX-style User Bank Request) might start a bank dump, and 45 00 00 (Preset Request, edit buffer) might answer. Both are read-only; the driver may offer them as an explicit 'try' action, never as probe().

driverNotes: TC Electronic G-Force: shares the 'tc' transport with the FireworX but has almost none of its SysEx. (1) WHAT EXISTS: program change + CC0 bank select; CC (or pitch bend / aftertouch / note / program change) into the I/O Setup Control assignments: Ext 1-8, main volume, overall bypass, tempo tap, tuner, 9 block bypasses; one SysEx exchange = the whole user bank as a bulk dump that the USER starts on the front panel. No edit-buffer request, no preset dump, no parameter SysEx is documented (MIDI chart: SysEx 'O Bulkdump'). (2) sendParam(p, v): p.path == 'cc' -> midi.cc(channel, p.cc, v). That is the whole real-time surface: Ext knobs move whatever the current preset's Matrix links them to (up to 20 links, per preset); block bypass CCs switch blocks. p.path == 'none' (all preset/block/modifier params) -> no-op; the editor should show these as offline/reference (they document the unit, and become live only if a future dump map appears). (3) sendPatch / requestPatch / requestProgram / writeProgram: unsupported -> throw 'the G-Force has no preset SysEx' (banks all have dump:false, write:false). requestName: unsupported. (4) probe(): nothing can be requested. Resolve true if anything has been received from the unit this session (bypass-status CCs after a program change are the easiest: send programChange to the current preset and wait 500 ms for CCs on the configured bypass numbers -- they arrive only if MIDI OUT is cabled and Control assignments exist); otherwise reject with 'no reply -- the G-Force only talks back after a preset change (block bypass CCs) or a front-panel bulk dump'. (5) programChange(bi, prog): midi.cc(ch, 0, bank.msb); midi.send([C0|ch, prog]). Needs Mapping mode External + Bank size 100 + Coarse (setup). CC0 values: 0 ROM 1-100, 1 ROM 101-200, 2 ROM 201-225, 3 user, 4-9 card banks 1-6. (6) decode(ev): CC on the basic channel matching a live param's cc -> [{param, value}]. After every preset change the unit sends each block's bypass state on its CC (1.13+); use it to update the bypass toggles and to learn the polarity (value for 'bypassed'). Program changes arriving from the unit (re-transmit option) can update the current slot. Ignore tuner traffic. (7) BULK DUMP CAPTURE (backup): arm a listener, tell the user to press Utility > User bank to MIDI, Enter, Enter. Expect (inferred from the FireworX format + Jacobsson's byte counts): header F0 00 20 1F dd MM 10 nH nL F7 announcing n packets, then n x F0 00 20 1F dd MM 11 id <128 nibble bytes> ck F7 (138 bytes; 64 data bytes each; ck = (-sum of the 64 data bytes) & 7F). Validate every packet's length and checksum; learn MM (model ID, prefs 'model') and dd from the header. Save all messages concatenated as one .syx. Allow ~60 s (the unit paces itself). If any packet is short/bad, discard the backup -- a corrupt dump sent back makes the unit erase its user bank. (8) RESTORE: only from a validated capture. User arms the unit (Utility > MIDI to User Bank, Enter; Tuner MIDI Out off; protect off); send header then packets unchanged, >= 150 ms apart. Overwrites all 100 user presets. (9) PACING: gapMs 20 for CCs; coalesce Ext knob drags to the editor's normal rate (CC is cheap, the unit smooths with the link Glide time). (10) UNTESTED OPTIONS (never automatic): with MM learned, FireworX-style requests (40 bank request; 45 00 00 preset request) might work on this platform; they are read-only, so the driver may expose them as a manual 'try' that reports whatever comes back.
